title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.29% in October as fuel and power prices jump 33%
dek: Crude oil and natural gas prices were up almost 71% on a year earlier, provisional government data show. The figure adds to pressure on the RBI after retail inflation crossed 6%.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's wholesale price inflation rose to 12.29% in October from 11.39% in September, driven mainly by a sharp rise in fuel and power prices linked to the West Asia conflict, according to provisional figures released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Monday.

The fuel and power index was 32.84% higher than a year earlier, up from 25.85% in September. Within it, crude petroleum and natural gas prices rose 70.80% and mineral oils, which include petrol, diesel and other refined products, 45.57%, according to the data as reported. Electricity prices rose 8.06%, after falling 0.43% in September.

## Where prices are rising

- Fuel and power: 32.84% (September: 25.85%)
- Primary articles: 9.24% (8.67%)
- Manufactured products: 9.54% (9.76%)
- WPI Food Index: 8.58% (8.66%)
- Basic metals: 17.21%; chemicals and chemical products: 17.53%

The ministry named mineral oils, crude petroleum and natural gas, electricity, food articles, basic metals, chemicals and food products as the main reasons for the rise, reports said. The all-commodities index, which now uses 2022-23 as its base year, rose to 113.3 from 112.5 in September. The October figure is provisional and was compiled from a weighted response rate of 81.1%, so it may be revised.

For April to October, wholesale inflation averaged 10.14%, compared with -0.30% in the same period last year, when wholesale prices were falling. Fuel and power inflation over the seven months was 26.37%.

## Background

Wholesale prices measure what producers and traders pay, and changes in them usually feed through to shop prices over the following months. The jump in energy costs dates from the war that began on 28 February between the US and Israel on one side and Iran on the other, and the disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, through which a large share of India's crude and cooking gas imports normally pass. Iranian forces have claimed several attacks on tankers in the past week.

The government has said it is absorbing most of the increase in diesel costs. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said last week that it had passed on only Rs 7 of a Rs 50-a-litre rise in diesel costs to consumers, at a loss of Rs 14,000 crore a month. That has kept retail fuel prices well below what the wholesale data would suggest.

Retail inflation, which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) targets, rose to 6.09% in October, above the upper end of its 2-6% tolerance band, according to data released on Thursday. Markets fell on Friday as traders priced in the chance of tighter policy.

## What happens next

Economists will be watching whether the RBI's monetary policy committee responds at its next meeting. Higher wholesale costs for metals and chemicals, which are inputs for many industries, suggest manufacturers' margins will be squeezed or that more increases will reach consumers. Shares rose on Monday morning as crude prices eased, with the Sensex up about 0.5% at midday, according to market reports. The final wholesale figure for October will be published in two months.
